maya: Anyone else hitting the python async client ignoring custom CA bundle when using a base_url that points at a Dedicated/private endpoint behind an HTTP proxy?

ev an: yep, saw that. quick repro I cobbled together: 
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(base_url="https://private.redwood.internal", api_key=MY_KEY, proxies={"http": "http://10.0.0.5:3128"}, ca_certs="/etc/ssl/custom-root.pem")
await client.text.generate("hello")
```
It still fails with ssl.SSLCertVerificationError against the upstream because the proxy terminates TLS to their CA.

sam: I had the same. Looks like the sync client honors REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / SSL_CERT_FILE but the async path doesn't wire the SSLContext into the aiohttp connector.

leigh: To add, mypy throws a typing mismatch when I tried to pass an SSLContext directly to AsyncClient: signature doesn't expose connector/ssl args for async client atm. So two bugs: runtime CA handling + missing typing surface.

maya: Reproduced locally. Setting env var SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/custom-root.pem and forcing trust_env on the process helps some runs but not when base_url resolves to an internal hostname via private DNS. Proxy chaining + aiohttp weirdness.

evan: Quick workaround that worked for me (ugly): create an aiohttp.ClientSession and pass in connector with SSLContext, then call into the client's lower-level session attribute:
```py
import ssl
from aiohttp import TCPConnector, ClientSession
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile="/etc/ssl/custom-root.pem")
conn = TCPConnector(ssl=ctx)
session = ClientSession(connector=conn)
client = AsyncClient._from_session(session, base_url=BASE)  # not public API
```
Not ideal but it proves the root cause.

sam: Yeah that matches my debugging. Also noticed the client sets trust_env=False inside the async constructor which prevents env proxy/CA plumbing; in sync path we rely on requests' trust_env default (True) unless overridden.

leigh: I'll open a PR to: (1) add explicit async kwargs: ssl_context, trust_env, proxies; (2) update types so mypy sees them; (3) fallback to honoring SSL_CERT_FILE / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE if ca_certs not passed.

maya: That sounds perfect. Can you include a short integration test that spins up a tiny proxy (mitmproxy in proxy mode) and verifies the client uses the provided CA? Even a smoke test that conditionally runs in CI would help prevent regressions.

ci-bot: test/async-proxy-ca (linux) queued ·  ↺

evan: For docs: we should document the precedence: explicit ca_certs param > SSLContext param > SSL_CERT_FILE env > system store, and also call out 'base_url + http proxy + private DNS' as a footgun.

leigh: Created issue #3407 and draft PR branch fix/async-ssl-proxy-3407. Will push tests later today. cc @maya @evan for review.

maya: Thanks! If you want, I can add a short example snippet to the onboarding quickstart that shows using SSL_CERT_FILE and the TLS tip for Dedicated customers. Saves support tickets. :thumbsup:

sam: One more note: we should also check the retry/backoff logic: if proxy returns a 502 during TLS handshake we currently treat it like a retriable 5xx which masks the root certificate error. That made debugging confusing.

leigh: Good call — adding a non-retriable classification for SSL verification failures in the transport layer.

maya: Awesome. Leaving this thread here. Follow-ups in PR + issue. :rocket:
